page.description: A predictable annual license. Your data stays yours.
page.usageHelp: Certificates and keys are not counted.
page.rule1: Review the customer, validity period and target limit before activation.
page.rule2: Annual licenses keep full operation during the grace period. After it, certificates already managed keep renewing for 45 more days. Evaluation licenses have no grace period.
page.rule3: Lock mode does not delete keys or revoke certificates. In-flight changes finish or roll back safely.
page.lockedText: Inventory, exports, the audit trail and backups remain available. Renew the license to resume changes.
page.continuityText_one: External changes are paused. So that your websites do not go down, certificates Alice already manages keep renewing and are deployed automatically to the places they are bound to until {{date}} ({{count}} day left). After that this stops too. Renew the license to resume everything.
page.continuityText_other: External changes are paused. So that your websites do not go down, certificates Alice already manages keep renewing and are deployed automatically to the places they are bound to until {{date}} ({{count}} days left). After that this stops too. Renew the license to resume everything.
page.continuityEnded: Automatic renewal and deployment of certificates stopped on {{date}}: certificates that expire from now on are not replaced.
page.graceText: Full operation continues until {{date}}. Then external changes pause; inventory, exports, the audit trail and backups stay available.
page.evaluationText: An evaluation has no grace period: when it ends, external changes pause until a signed license is uploaded.

capabilities.title: What Alice can do with it
capabilities.description: Depends on where the certificate comes from.

yes.discover: Alice finds where it is used, on your servers and on the network.
yes.obtain: Alice gets it from its certificate authority herself.
yes.renew: Alice renews it before it expires.
yes.deploy: Alice can put it on your servers.
yes.verify: After a deployment Alice checks that the server serves it.
yes.revoke: Alice can ask its certificate authority to revoke it.
yes.recovery: After an outage of the authority, the DNS or a hook, Alice resumes its renewal by herself.

no.discover: Alice does not look for it.
no.obtain: It comes from outside Alice: someone brought it, or a key vault or a server holds it.
no.renew: Alice does not renew it; its issuer (or Azure Key Vault) does.
no.deploy: Alice does not hold its private key, so she cannot deploy it.
no.verify: Alice checks only what she deploys.
no.revoke: Alice did not order it from a certificate authority, so only its issuing authority can revoke it.
no.recovery: Alice does not renew it, so there is no renewal to recover.

verify_failed.action: Check which binding answers for this website's name and port on the server (netsh http show sslcert, and the site's bindings in IIS Manager), then deploy again.

interrupted.cause: While the deployment ran, the connection to the server was lost, Alice restarted, or the helper could not finish changing the binding. The deployment's status shows which certificate the binding names; if Alice does not know yet, it keeps checking.

verify_chain.cause: The number of certificates the website sends differs from the chain Alice expected, for example because Windows built the chain from other intermediate certificates in its stores, or a proxy adds or drops some. The deployment's status shows whether anything was changed.
verify_chain.action: Check the intermediate certificates in the server's Intermediate Certification Authorities store and anything in front of the server, then deploy again.

verify_untrusted.action: Check the intermediate certificates in the server's Intermediate Certification Authorities store, and that nothing in front of the server (a proxy or a load balancer) sends another chain, then deploy again.

nothing_to_restore.cause: The helper found that this deployment had not changed the binding, so there was nothing to put back.

superseded.title: A later change replaced the binding, so Alice did not restore it.
superseded.cause: While Alice was finishing this deployment, a later operation on the server changed the binding. Alice cannot tell which certificate it names now.

target_deleted.action: If the server still exists, check its website and the certificate its binding names.

recovery_exhausted.cause: For about a day Alice could not find out how the deployment ended, usually because it could not reach the server. If the change reached the server, the previous certificate is still in its certificate store.

outcome_unknown.cause: Alice no longer has the records it needs to check or undo this deployment. If the change reached the server, the previous certificate is still in its certificate store.

rescan_needed.title: Alice must read this server's bindings again before deploying.
rescan_needed.cause: Alice does not know which certificate the binding names now, which it needs to make sure nobody changed the binding in the meantime.

pending_change_restored.title: Alice undid an unfinished earlier change of this binding; this certificate was not deployed.
pending_change_restored.cause: An earlier change of this binding on the server did not finish, and Alice no longer followed it. Alice pointed the binding back to the certificate from before that change, so the website now serves that certificate. The certificate of this deployment was not deployed.
pending_change_restored.action: Choose Discover on the server's page so that Alice reads the bindings again, then deploy the certificate again.

server_operation_pending.title: An unfinished change of this binding on the server stops new changes.
server_operation_pending.cause: An earlier change of this binding on the server did not finish, and Alice no longer follows it, so the helper refuses new changes. Alice did not undo that change. This deployment's certificate was not deployed.
server_operation_pending.action: The deployment's details name the unfinished change (operation id). Check which certificate the binding names (netsh http show sslcert), choose Discover on the server's page, then deploy again.

rollback_forbidden.cause: The new certificate could not be put in service, and the certificate the binding named before the change was revoked or its private key is compromised. Alice never binds such a certificate again, so the binding stays as the failed change left it. The website may not work until another certificate is deployed.
rollback_forbidden.action: Check the website now. Find and fix the cause shown in the deployment history (the binding or the check of the website), then deploy a valid certificate again or choose Retry on the incident. Never point the binding back to the previous certificate by hand: its key is compromised.

location_unsupported.cause: The binding is one Alice does not change (it belongs to another application, or its certificate or store does not meet Alice's rules), or it no longer exists. Nothing was changed.

output_too_large.action: Check the server for unusually large content in what Alice reads there: the http.sys bindings, the IIS configuration or the certificate stores.

protocol_error.action: Copy alice-helper.exe from the current Alice bundle to the server and run the Windows setup script again, then test the connection.

register.emailHelp: The authority may send notices to this address, for example about problems with your certificates.
register.tos: I have read and accept the terms at this address
register.tosHelp: The authority publishes these terms. The account is registered for exactly these terms; if the authority changes them before you register, Alice shows the new ones.
register.done: The account is registered. You can now get certificates from this authority.
register.contacting: Contacting {{host}} to read its terms of service…
register.previewFailed: Alice could not read the terms of the certificate authority, so the account cannot be registered yet.
register.termsChangedText: The authority changed its terms after they were shown here. Nothing was registered. Read the new terms below and accept them again.
register.eabRequiredTitle: This authority needs an external account binding
register.eabRequiredText: The authority only accepts accounts with a key ID and a secret key from your account with them, and none is stored. Edit the certificate authority and enter both first, or the registration will be refused.
register.unsafeTitle: The terms cannot be shown safely
register.unsafeText: The authority publishes its terms at an address that is not a safe https address, so Alice does not show it and does not register an account. Ask the authority, or check that the directory address is right.
register.noTerms: This authority publishes no terms of service. The account can be registered without accepting any.

rollover.title: Rotate the account key for {{name}}?
rollover.text: Alice creates a new account key and asks the authority to use it instead of the current one. The account and its certificates stay the same. Do this when the key may be known to someone else, or as part of your regular key changes.

deactivate.title: Deactivate the account with {{name}}?
deactivate.text: The authority will never accept this account again. This cannot be undone. To use the authority afterwards, register a new account.
deactivate.affectedMore_one: More than {{count}} certificate uses this authority.
deactivate.affectedMore_other: More than {{count}} certificates use this authority.
deactivate.affectedText: They are not renewed until a new account is registered. The certificates already on your servers keep working until they expire.

hook.intro: A DNS hook is a small service of yours that adds the proof record to your DNS for Alice and removes it again. "How does the hook work?" below describes the calls it receives.
hook.name: Name shown in Alice
hook.urlHelp: The https:// address Alice calls. It cannot contain a user name or password.
hook.secretHelp: {{min}} to {{max}} characters. Alice sends it with every call, so that your hook knows the call comes from Alice. Use a long random value and set the same value in the hook.
hook.secretKept: A secret is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
hook.secretRequired: Enter the secret that the hook expects.
hook.bundle: Root certificate of the hook's CA (optional)
hook.bundleHelp: Only needed when the hook's https certificate comes from your own internal CA. Paste the public certificate (PEM).
hook.waitHelp: How long Alice waits after the hook added the record before the authority checks it: 0 to {{max}} seconds.
hook.poll: Time to wait for the record (seconds)
hook.pollHelp: How long Alice keeps asking the hook whether the record is visible: {{min}} to {{max}} seconds. Both times together are at most {{total}} seconds.
hook.waitRange: Enter a whole number from 0 to {{max}}.
hook.pollRange: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
hook.totalRange: Both times together can be at most {{max}} seconds.
hook.noContactText: Alice only stores these settings. The hook is called when a certificate is ordered.
hook.deleteText: Alice forgets the settings of this hook. This is only possible when no certificate uses it.

help.title: How does the hook work?
help.request: For each name, Alice sends the hook an HTTPS POST request with a small JSON body: first with "action": "present" to add the TXT record, and after the check with "action": "cleanup" to remove exactly that record again.
help.body: The body also has the record's name in "fqdn" (for example _acme-challenge.example.com), its "value" and a "ttl". A wildcard name and its base name use the same record name, so keep both values side by side.
help.auth: Every call carries the secret twice: in the header Authorization: Bearer <secret>, and in X-Alice-Signature, an HMAC-SHA256 of the exact body made with the secret, in lowercase hex. Check either one, or both.
help.answer: Answer 200 or 204 when done; any other answer is a refusal. While the record is not visible yet you may answer {"ready": false}: Alice then asks again until you answer {"ready": true}. Repeating a call must do no harm.
help.limits: Alice waits up to {{wait}} seconds after a record is added and asks for at most {{poll}} seconds, {{total}} seconds in all.

dns.intro: Alice signs in to your DNS provider and adds the proof record itself, then removes it again. The credentials need only the right to change the records of the zones below.
dns.tokenRule: The token needs {{min}} to {{max}} characters without spaces.
dns.groupRule: Use up to 90 letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, dots or brackets, not ending with a dot.
dns.keyRequired: Paste the private key that belongs to this certificate.
dns.accessKeyRule: Enter the access key ID: 16 to 128 capital letters and digits.
dns.secretKeyRule: The secret access key needs {{min}} to {{max}} characters without spaces.
dns.roleRule: Enter a role ARN like arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/name.
dns.kept: Credentials are stored. Leave this empty to keep them.
dns.apiTokenHelp: An API token (not the Global API Key) with Zone Read and DNS Edit for the zones of these names.
dns.clientOptional: Client ID of a user-assigned identity (optional)
dns.clientOptionalHelp: Leave this empty for the system-assigned identity of the machine Alice runs on.
dns.certStored: Stored certificate: thumbprint {{thumbprint}}. Paste a new one only to replace it.
dns.certificateHelp: The public certificate you uploaded to the app registration, and below its RSA private key.
dns.resourceGroup: Resource group of the DNS zones
dns.roleHelp: An IAM role ARN. Alice then works with the role's temporary credentials.

permissions.cloudflare: A Cloudflare API token with the permissions Zone → Zone → Read and Zone → DNS → Edit, limited to the zones Alice may use.
permissions.azure_dns: The role "DNS Zone Contributor" on the zone or the resource group, and Reader on the resource group to find the zone. Public DNS zones only.
permissions.route53: An IAM policy with route53:ListHostedZonesByName, route53:ListResourceRecordSets, route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets and route53:GetChange (and sts:AssumeRole on the role, if one is given). Public hosted zones only.

dns.waitHelp: How long Alice waits after the provider reports the record as live, before the authority checks it: 0 to {{max}} seconds.
dns.pollHelp: How long Alice waits for the provider to report the record as live (Route 53 reports when every server has it): {{min}} to {{max}} seconds. Both times together are at most {{total}} seconds.
dns.noContactText: Alice only stores these settings and the credentials, encrypted. The provider is first contacted when a certificate is ordered.

challenge.http01: Web proof (file on the web server)

issued.title: Issued certificates
issued.description: Certificates that Alice gets and renews by itself from a certificate authority, through automatic certificate issuance (ACME).
issued.detailDescription: A certificate Alice gets and renews from a certificate authority.
issued.readOnly: You can look, not change. Operators and administrators act on these certificates.
issued.adminOnly: Only an administrator can change this.
issued.lockedTitle: The license does not allow changes now
issued.lockedText: While the license is expired or cannot be checked, Alice does not contact a certificate authority or a server: getting, testing and deploying certificates waits. In the first 45 days of a lock, certificates already issued are still renewed and deployed automatically. Removing a website or a certificate still works.
issued.lockedShort: The license does not allow this now.
issued.empty: No certificates from a certificate authority yet
issued.emptyText: Alice can get a certificate for your names from a certificate authority, such as Let's Encrypt or your company's own CA, renew it before it expires and put it on your websites.
issued.emptyNoAuthority: First add a certificate authority and register an account with it:
issued.noMatchText: Change or clear the filters to see more.
issued.testRunHelp: A Test run checks that the certificate authority can verify your names. Nothing is issued or installed.
issued.rearmed: Automatic renewal is on again. Alice renews the certificate at the next planned time. To renew right now, use {{order}}.
issued.orderRunning: Alice is talking to the certificate authority. This page updates by itself.
issued.deployHelp: Choose the websites that get the current certificate now, at most {{max}} at a time. Each gets its own deployment, which you can follow on the Deployments page.
issued.deleteText: Alice stops renewing it and forgets which websites follow it. The websites keep the certificate they serve now, and the issued certificates stay in the certificate list.

renewal.title: Renewal
renewal.autoHelpOn: Alice renews this certificate by itself before it expires and keeps trying after a failure, with growing waits.
renewal.autoHelpOff: Alice does not renew this certificate by itself. Someone has to order a new one before it expires.
renewal.plannedAri: {{date}} (a time Alice chose in the window the authority suggests)
renewal.ariNote: Alice chose this time at random inside the window the certificate authority suggests, so that certificates do not all reach the authority at the same moment. It keeps the time until the authority moves its window, and never renews later than this certificate's own renewal setting allows.
renewal.afterFirst: After the first certificate is issued
renewal.failingText_one: The last attempt failed. Alice tries again by itself.
renewal.failingText_other: The last {{count}} attempts failed. Alice tries again by itself.
renewal.failingNext_one: The last attempt failed. Alice tries again at {{time}}.
renewal.failingNext_other: The last {{count}} attempts failed. Alice tries again at {{time}}.
renewal.stoppedText_one: Alice stopped renewing this certificate by itself after {{count}} failed attempt, because the cause needs a person, so that it does not keep asking the certificate authority in vain.
renewal.stoppedText_other: Alice stopped renewing this certificate by itself after {{count}} failed attempts in a row, because the cause needs a person, so that it does not keep asking the certificate authority in vain.
renewal.stoppedAdmin: Fix the problem below, then choose Check again and resume: Alice orders the certificate at once and renews it by itself again. {{order}} also renews it at once. A Test run first shows whether the names can be verified.
renewal.stoppedOperator: Fix the problem below and use Test run or {{order}}. Only an administrator can resume automatic renewal (Check again and resume).
renewal.stoppedAuditor: An administrator can resume automatic renewal with Check again and resume.
renewal.transientText: The cause looks temporary: the certificate authority or the DNS service could not be reached, did not answer in time or limited the requests. Alice keeps trying by itself, at least once a day and more often as the certificate nears its end.
renewal.permanentText_one: The cause needs a person (for example a setting, the account at the certificate authority or a refused name). If {{count}} more attempt fails like this, Alice stops trying by itself.
renewal.permanentText_other: The cause needs a person (for example a setting, the account at the certificate authority or a refused name). If {{count}} more attempts fail like this, Alice stops trying by itself.
renewal.recoveringText_one: Alice stopped after {{count}} failed attempt, but the last problem was a temporary outage: Alice still tries again by itself, at least once a day, until the certificate expires.
renewal.recoveringText_other: Alice stopped after {{count}} failed attempts in a row, but the last problem was a temporary outage: Alice still tries again by itself, at least once a day, until the certificate expires.
renewal.caWaitText: The certificate authority asked Alice to wait until {{time}}. Alice does not order this certificate before then, neither by itself nor with {{order}} or Test run, because ordering sooner only makes the wait longer.
renewal.caWaitCritical: Little time is left after this wait: the current certificate ends at {{end}}. The administrators were e-mailed. If the certificate cannot wait, get one from another certificate authority and upload it.

notice.pending_one: Still being tried for {{pending}} of {{count}} recipient (last error: {{code}}; {{time}})
notice.pending_other: Still being tried for {{pending}} of {{count}} recipients (last error: {{code}}; {{time}})
notice.noServer: Not sent: no mail server is set ({{time}})

test.ok: Test run succeeded: the authority verified every name
test.okText: Nothing was issued or installed. You can get the certificate now.
test.failedNoReason: The authority did not verify the names. Look at the orders below.

orders.title: Orders
orders.description: The last requests to the certificate authority, newest first.

current.title: Current certificate
current.noneText: Use Test run to check your names, then Get certificate now.
current.chainIncomplete: Incomplete: an administrator confirms before it is deployed

bindings.title: Websites using this certificate
bindings.description: Where Alice puts this certificate, and what each website serves now.
bindings.notIssued: Websites come after the first certificate
bindings.notIssuedText: Once the certificate is issued, connect the websites that should use it here.
bindings.none: No website is connected to this certificate yet.
bindings.certAutoOn: After each renewal, Alice deploys the new certificate by itself to the websites below whose own automatic deployment is on.
bindings.certAutoOff: New certificates are not deployed by themselves. Use Deploy now, or ask an administrator to switch this on.
bindings.autoSummary_one: Will deploy automatically to {{n}} of {{count}} website.
bindings.autoSummary_other: Will deploy automatically to {{n}} of {{count}} websites.
bindings.autoCertOnly: The certificate's automatic deployment is on, but no website below has its own automatic deployment on, so nothing is deployed by itself.
bindings.autoSitesOnly_one: {{count}} website has its own automatic deployment on, but the certificate's automatic deployment is off, so nothing is deployed by itself.
bindings.autoSitesOnly_other: {{count}} websites have their own automatic deployment on, but the certificate's automatic deployment is off, so nothing is deployed by itself.
bindings.servedNone: Does not serve a certificate from here yet.
bindings.autoAdminOnly: Only an administrator can switch automatic deployment on. You can switch it off.
bindings.autoConfirmCert: Alice then deploys each renewed certificate by itself to the websites whose own automatic deployment is on, in small groups, and stops after repeated failures.
bindings.autoConfirmSite: Alice then deploys each renewed certificate to this website by itself:
bindings.autoConfirmStepUp: You confirm it's you with a fresh code.
bindings.byHandTitle: Changing one of these websites by hand
bindings.byHand: Remove the website here, or switch off its automatic deployment and choose Report only for its changes, before you change its certificate by hand. Otherwise Alice may put this certificate back at the next renewal or, with automatic repair, at the next check.
bindings.heldTitle: Automatic deployment is waiting for an administrator
bindings.heldAdmin: This certificate was issued while the license did not allow changes. Check it, then choose Release so that automatic deployment may use it, or use Deploy now.
bindings.heldOther: This certificate was issued while the license did not allow changes. An administrator checks it and releases it, or you use Deploy now.
bindings.heldChainTitle: Automatic deployment is holding this certificate
bindings.heldChainAdmin: Its certificate chain is incomplete, so Alice does not deploy it by itself. Check it, then use Deploy now and confirm the chain.
bindings.heldChainOther: Its certificate chain is incomplete, so Alice does not deploy it by itself. An administrator checks it and deploys it with Deploy now.
bindings.stoppedText: Automatic deployment of this certificate stopped after repeated failures. Look at the websites that need attention, fix the cause, then use Deploy now.
bindings.addHelp: Choose the websites that should use this certificate. Only websites on Nginx and Windows (IIS) servers whose key type fits are listed. Automatic deployment starts off for each of them.
bindings.noLocations: No website fits this certificate's key type, or every one already uses it.
bindings.followsVault: Follows a Key Vault certificate. Disconnect it there first.
bindings.partlyAdded_one: {{count}} website was connected before Alice stopped at the marked one; the rest were not tried.
bindings.partlyAdded_other: {{count}} websites were connected before Alice stopped at the marked one; the rest were not tried.
bindings.removeTitle: Remove this website from the certificate?
bindings.removeText: The website keeps the certificate it serves now. Alice no longer deploys this certificate to it.

names.tooLong: A name can have at most 253 characters.
names.twoLabels: Use a full name with at least two parts, such as "www.example.com".
names.invalid: Use only letters, digits, hyphens and dots. A part cannot start or end with a hyphen.
names.wildcardPlace: A wildcard (*) can only be the whole first part, such as "*.example.com".
names.address: Use a name, not an IP address.
names.duplicate: This name is already in the list.
names.tooMany: A certificate can have at most 100 names.

wizard.title: Get a certificate

heading.names: Which names should the certificate cover?
heading.proof: How does Alice prove that you control the names?

wizard.authorityHelp: The authority issues the certificate. Only authorities with a registered account can be chosen.
wizard.noAccount: No account is registered with this authority yet.
wizard.rolloverPending: The account key change of this authority is not settled yet.
wizard.noNames: No names are allowed for this authority yet.
wizard.noAuthorityText: Add a certificate authority, register an account with it and allow the domain endings you need:
wizard.namesHelp: Add each name the certificate should cover. Visitors' browsers check that the website's name is in this list.
wizard.name: Name
wizard.nameHelp: For example "www.example.com". Press Enter or Add after each name.
wizard.wildcardHint: A wildcard name (*.example.com) can only be proven with the DNS proof.
wizard.notAllowedProvider: These names are outside the domain endings allowed for {{authority}}. Alice will refuse them unless an administrator adds the endings in Settings:
wizard.notAllowedHook: These names are outside the domain endings allowed for {{hook}}:
wizard.dnsHelp: A DNS hook, a small service of yours, adds a temporary record to your DNS. Works for every name, including wildcards.
wizard.httpHelp: Web site file proof (HTTP-01): Alice puts a small file on one of your servers that can publish it (today, Nginx servers), and the authority reads it over port 80. The names must point at that server.
wizard.wildcardNeedsDns: A wildcard name needs the DNS proof.
wizard.chooseHookOption: Choose a DNS provider or hook
wizard.chooseHook: Choose a DNS provider or hook.
wizard.noHookTitle: No DNS provider or hook yet
wizard.noHookText: An administrator adds a DNS provider or hook first:
wizard.serverHelp: The server that answers for these names on port 80 and can publish the file (today, an Nginx server).
wizard.noServer: No server in Alice can publish an HTTP-01 challenge yet. Add an Nginx server, or choose DNS validation.
wizard.prepareText: Alice never changes your Nginx configuration. Add these lines to the server block that listens on port 80 for the names, then check and reload Nginx yourself:
wizard.prepareDoc: The guide "Preparing an Nginx server" (section "Publishing HTTP-01 challenges") explains the folder Alice uses and how to check it.
wizard.helperHint: If the order says the helper on the server is too old for this proof method, copy alice-helper from the current Alice bundle to the server and run the preparation again.
wizard.keyTypeHelp: ECDSA P-256 suits almost every website. Choose RSA only for very old clients.
wizard.renewBefore: Renew how many days before it expires
wizard.renewBeforeHelp: 1 to 60 days. For short-lived certificates Alice renews earlier, at a third of the lifetime at the latest.
wizard.renewRange: Use a whole number from 1 to 60.
wizard.autoRenewHelp: Alice renews the certificate before it expires, without anyone asking.
wizard.autoDeployHelp: After each renewal, Alice deploys the new certificate by itself to the connected websites whose own automatic deployment is on. You confirm it's you when you save.
wizard.websitesLater: You connect the websites on the certificate's page once the first certificate is issued.
wizard.reviewHelp: Saving orders nothing yet. You confirm it's you with a fresh code.
wizard.testHelp: A Test run (recommended) checks that the authority can verify your names, without issuing anything. Or get the certificate now.

issued.rearmedOrdered: Automatic renewal is on again, and Alice is ordering the certificate now. The orders below show how it goes.

revoke.title: Revoke the certificate?
revoke.text: Alice asks the certificate authority to revoke the certificate. This cannot be undone: browsers may refuse it from then on, and Alice never deploys it again.
revoke.leakedText: Then start a key compromise incident from the certificate's page instead: Alice first replaces it everywhere with a certificate made with a new key, and revokes it afterwards.
revoke.understood: I understand that a revocation cannot be undone.
revoke.doneRenew: Automatic renewal is on: Alice orders a new certificate shortly. Deploy it where the revoked one is still served.
revoke.doneNoRenew: Automatic renewal is off: order a new certificate with Order now and deploy it where the revoked one is still served.

discovery.title: Network discovery
discovery.description: Certificates Alice finds when it connects to the addresses you list. A scan only reads the certificate a server presents: it never changes anything on the scanned servers.
discovery.readOnly: You can look, not change. Operators start and cancel scans; administrators decide what is scanned.
discovery.operatorNote: Only an administrator defines scopes and the discovery settings. You can start and cancel scans.
discovery.lockedTitle: The license does not allow scans now
discovery.lockedText: While the license is expired or cannot be checked, Alice starts no scan and scheduled scans wait. You can still see the results, cancel a scan and change scopes.

empty.title: Nothing is scanned until you add a scope
empty.text: A scope lists the addresses, ranges and host names Alice may connect to, and the ports to try. During a scan Alice opens a secure (TLS) connection to each of them, reads the certificate the server presents and closes the connection. It sends nothing else and never changes the scanned servers.
empty.who: Administrators define scopes and the discovery settings. Operators and administrators start and cancel scans. Auditors can see everything.

unmanagedHelp.title: What “unmanaged” means
unmanagedHelp.text: Unmanaged means Alice has no record of this exact certificate. A certificate in front of servers that Alice manages, for example on a proxy or a load balancer, is still unmanaged unless Alice stores that same certificate.

statusText.unmanaged: Alice has no record of this exact certificate.
statusText.managed: Alice has this certificate, and it is in use on a server that Alice manages.
statusText.known: Alice has this certificate in its inventory, but not on any server that Alice manages now.

endpointError.timeout: There was no answer in time.
endpointError.no_tls: The server did not complete a TLS handshake.
endpointError.reset: The connection was closed during the handshake.
endpointError.chain_too_large: The server sent a certificate chain too large to record.
endpointError.policy: Not scanned: the address is excluded or outside the allowed scan networks.
endpointError.malformed: The server sent a certificate Alice cannot read.

results.label: Certificates found on the network
results.searchHelp: A name or a part of it
results.noResultsText: Start a scan of a scope on the Scans tab. The certificates it finds appear here.
results.noResultsRead: The certificates found by the scans of a scope appear here.
results.noMatchText: Change or clear the filters to see more.

drawer.title: Certificate found on the network
drawer.subject: Name (CN)
drawer.endpointsHelp: Each place is an address and a port, and the server name Alice asked for, if any.
drawer.noEndpoints: No endpoint presents this certificate now.
drawer.moreEndpoints: Only the first 200 places are shown.
drawer.addServerHelp: Opens the Add server dialog with this address filled in. A new server counts toward your license; Alice checks the license when you add it.
drawer.adminAdds: An administrator can add this server to Alice.

scopes.title: Scan scopes
scopes.description: What Alice may scan, and when.
scopes.emptyText: Add a scope to tell Alice which addresses and ports it may scan. Nothing is scanned until then.
scopes.emptyOther: An administrator adds scopes. Nothing is scanned until then.

schedule.rounded_one: With a daily time window, {{hours}} hours count as whole days: every day.
schedule.rounded_other: With a daily time window, {{hours}} hours count as whole days: every {{count}} days.

block.locked: The license does not allow scans now.
block.noNetworks: No allowed scan networks are set, so nothing can be scanned.
block.running: A scan of this scope is already running.
block.tooMany: Two scans are already running. Wait until one has finished.
block.noneReady: No scope can be scanned now: each one is switched off or already being scanned.

settings.title: Discovery settings
settings.allowedHelp: Alice scans only addresses inside these networks. One IP address or range per line, for example 10.0.0.0/16. An empty list means nothing is scanned.
settings.exclusionsHelp: Addresses and ranges that no scope may scan. One per line.
settings.retentionHelp: Places that are not found again are removed after this many days. From {{min}} to {{max}} days.
settings.retentionRange: Enter a whole number of days from {{min}} to {{max}}.
settings.builtinHelp: Alice never scans these, whatever the settings say: its own addresses, the database, loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses and other reserved ranges.
settings.emptyTitle: Nothing is scanned until you list the networks Alice may scan
settings.emptyText: A scan only reaches addresses inside the allowed scan networks. None are set yet, so no scope can be scanned.
settings.emptyOther: An administrator sets them in the discovery settings.

scope.name: Name
scope.entriesHelp: One per line: an IP address (10.0.0.5), a range (10.0.1.0/24, at most a /20; IPv6 at most a /120) or a host name. At most {{max}}.
scope.entriesRequired: Enter at least one address, range or host name.
scope.portsHelp: The ports to try, separated by commas, for example 443, 8443. At most {{max}}.
scope.portInvalid: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
scope.sniHelp: Some servers present a different certificate for each name. Alice asks for every name listed here at every address. A host name in the list above is asked for by itself. One per line.
scope.exclusionsHelp: Addresses and ranges inside this scope that Alice must not scan. One per line.
scope.rangeProblem: Enter a whole number up to {{max}}, or leave it empty.
scope.hoursHelp: Empty: only when someone starts a scan. At most {{max}} hours (one week).
scope.hoursRange: Enter a whole number of hours from 0 to {{max}}.
scope.useWindow: Only scan during a daily time window
scope.windowHelp: A scan starts only inside the window. When the clocks change for daylight saving time, the window still closes at its local end time, so on that day it can be an hour shorter. With a window, an interval of 24 hours or more counts whole days: 36 hours means every 2 days.
scope.windowRequired: Enter a start and an end time that differ.
scope.windowNeedsSchedule: A time window needs a schedule: enter the hours between scans.
scope.alert: E-mail before certificates found by this scope expire
scope.alertHelp: Uses the expiry thresholds in Settings → Alerts. Only certificates that Alice does not manage are reported.
scope.enabledHelp: A scope that is switched off is not scanned, neither by its schedule nor by hand.
scope.noNetworks: No allowed scan networks are set yet, so this scope cannot be saved. Set them in the discovery settings first.
scope.runningTitle: A scan of this scope is running
scope.runningText: Changing the addresses, ports, server names or exclusions stops it. The results found until then are kept.

preview.title: Size of this scope
preview.waiting: Enter the addresses and ports to see the size.
preview.endpoints_one: One scan tries {{n}} combination of address, port and server name (at most {{max}}).
preview.endpoints_other: One scan tries {{n}} combinations of address, port and server name (at most {{max}}).
preview.excluded_one: {{n}} address is left out by the exclusions.
preview.excluded_other: {{n}} addresses are left out by the exclusions.
preview.builtin: Alice always leaves these out of the ranges here:
preview.stepUp: Confirm it is you to see the size.
preview.tooMany: Too many size checks; the size updates in a minute.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.text: Alice stops scanning these addresses. A scan of this scope that is running now is stopped.
delete.results: The places this scope found are removed by the regular cleanup. A certificate that another scope also finds stays in the results.

scans.title: Scans
scans.polling: The newest scans first. This list updates by itself while a scan runs.
scans.startHelp: Alice connects to every address and port of the scope and reads the certificates. It changes nothing on the scanned servers.
scans.noScopeReady: No scope can be scanned now
scans.noScopes: Add a scope on the Scopes tab first.
scans.emptyText: The scans of each scope appear here, started by hand or by the scope's schedule.
scans.countsHelp: Answered: the server completed a TLS handshake. Not answering: it refused the connection, did not answer in time or did not complete a TLS handshake.

directories.none: No directory is set up yet.
directories.max: Alice works with at most 3 directories.
directories.adminNote: SSO users may be Admin (on the Single sign-on tab) applies to directory users too: while it is off, directory users can be at most Operators.
directories.passwordNote: Directory passwords pass through Alice over a verified ldaps:// connection. They are never stored or logged.

presets.label: Fill in typical values
presets.help: A preset fills the attribute and filter fields only. Nothing is saved until you save the directory.

fields.name: Name shown on the sign-in page
fields.addressesHelp: One ldaps:// address per line, at most 3, tried in order. Example: ldaps://dc1.corp.example:636
fields.uniqueIdHelp: A value that never changes for a person: objectGUID in Active Directory, entryUUID in OpenLDAP. It cannot be changed once people have signed in.
fields.bindDnHelp: A read-only account Alice uses to find users and their groups.
fields.bindPasswordStored: A password is stored. Leave the field empty to keep it.
fields.bindPasswordReenter: You changed the addresses, the service account, the unique ID attribute or the certificate authority: enter the service account password again.
fields.groupNameHelp: Leave empty to use the group's DN as the group value.
fields.mfaRequired: Ask for Alice's authenticator code after the directory password

directories.templateRules: Filter rules: {login} and {dn} stand only in a value position, for example (uid={login}). Write a literal brace as \7b or \7d. Control characters are not allowed.
directories.deleteText: The directory, its group mappings and its stored password are removed. A directory that people have signed in through cannot be deleted: switch sign-in through it off instead.
directories.connectionOk: The connection works: Alice could bind as the service account and search the user base DN.
directories.testSignInText: Nobody is signed in and the password is not stored. The result shows the groups the directory returns and the role they give.

result.title: The directory accepted the sign-in.
result.noRole: None: no group is mapped, so this person cannot sign in.

directories.noMappings: No group is mapped yet. Without a mapping nobody can sign in through this directory.
directories.groupHelp: The value exactly as Test sign-in lists it: matched exactly and case-sensitively.
directories.removeMappingText: Members of this group no longer get this role at their next sign-in or confirmation.

incidents.title: Key compromise incident
incidents.adminOnly: Only an Administrator acts on an incident.
incidents.notRevocableTitle: Revoke it at the issuing authority
incidents.notRevocableText: Alice did not order this certificate from a certificate authority, so she cannot revoke it. Ask the authority that issued it to revoke it; Alice has marked it compromised and replaces it on your servers.

start.title: Start a key compromise incident?
start.intro: Use this when the private key of this certificate is no longer secret. Alice then:
start.stepMark: marks this certificate and every other certificate made with the same key as compromised, for good (they are never deployed again);
start.stepOrder: orders a new certificate from the certificate authority, with a new private key;
start.stepChoose: waits for you to choose the replacement: a certificate made with a new private key that you upload;
start.stepDeploy: deploys the replacement to every server file that holds this certificate, and checks each one;
start.stepRevoke: revokes this certificate at the certificate authority (reason: key compromise) once every replacement is verified.
start.stepNoRevoke: cannot revoke it: only the authority that issued it can.
start.notRevocableText: It does not come from an order Alice made. Ask the authority that issued it to revoke it.
start.revokeNow: Revoke at once, without waiting for the replacement
start.revokeNowHelp: Websites that still serve this certificate may stop working until the replacement is deployed.
start.understood: I understand that this cannot be undone.

busy.ordering: Alice is ordering the new certificate. This page updates itself.
busy.deploying: Alice is deploying the replacement. This page updates itself.
busy.revoking: Alice is revoking the compromised certificate. This page updates itself.

notice.ordering: A new certificate is being ordered
notice.revoking: The compromised certificate is being revoked

noticeText.awaiting_replacement: Upload a certificate made with a new private key, then choose it here. Alice deploys it to every affected place.
noticeText.ordering: The certificate authority is issuing a certificate with a new private key. Alice deploys it as soon as it arrives.
noticeText.deploying: Alice puts the replacement on every affected place and checks it. The compromised certificate is revoked afterwards.
noticeText.revoking: Every replacement is verified. Alice is asking the certificate authority to revoke the compromised certificate.
noticeText.completed: The replacement is deployed everywhere Alice could, and the compromised certificate is revoked where Alice can revoke it.
noticeText.closed: An administrator closed the incident. Places not replaced keep what they serve.

locations.title: Affected places
locations.description: Certificate files on managed servers that hold the compromised certificate or its key.
locations.none: No managed server holds the certificate. Check the network endpoints on the certificate's page.

close.title: Close the incident?
close.text: Alice stops working on it: no further deployment is requested and nothing more is revoked. Deployments already started go on. The certificates stay marked compromised.

revokeNow.title: Revoke now regardless?
revokeNow.text: Alice revokes the compromised certificate at its certificate authority now, without waiting for every replacement to be verified. Websites that still serve it may stop working. This cannot be undone.

replacement.title: Choose the replacement
replacement.text: Choose a certificate Alice holds the private key of, made with another key than the compromised one. Alice deploys it to every affected place.
replacement.uploadHint: Not listed? Upload it first on the Certificates page.

list.title: Key compromise incidents
list.description: Every key compromise incident, newest first.

services.title: Services

page.description: Every server, Key Vault, certificate and key belongs to one service. A service has an environment and a policy; trusts say which services may send certificates and keys to which.

services.deleteNotEmpty: Move its resources to another service first.
services.deleteText: The service and its policy are deleted. It owns nothing, so no server, certificate or key changes.

policy.title: Service policy
policy.description: The rules for what this service owns. The Policy tab shows and changes them.

move.intro: Alice first checks what the move would change. Nothing moves until you confirm.
move.nothing: It is already in that service: nothing would change.
move.untrustedTitle_one: {{count}} binding would no longer deploy automatically
move.untrustedTitle_other: {{count}} bindings would no longer deploy automatically
move.untrustedHelp: These bindings stay in place, but automatic deployment stops until the receiving service accepts certificates and keys from the sending one (Trusts).

trusts.intro: A binding across two services deploys automatically only when the receiving service accepts certificates and keys from the sending one.

dialog.environmentHelp: The environment decides which environment-wide access reaches this service.

filter.noMatch: Nothing in the chosen service or environment.

environments.name: Name
environments.keyHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It cannot change later.
environments.keyPattern: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter.

policyForm.intro: The policy decides what may enter this service and how its certificates behave. Every rule is optional: a rule left empty sets no limit. It applies to what is created or changed from now on, never to what exists, except that forbidding automatic deployment holds the deployments already switched on.

names.title: Names and sources
names.description: Which names this service's certificates may carry and how certificates may enter it.

policyForm.domainsHelp: One per line, at most {{max}}: a name (pay.example.com), a wildcard (*.pay.example.com covers every name below it, at any depth, but not pay.example.com itself), an IP address or a CIDR block (10.20.0.0/16). Empty: any name.
policyForm.domainsGlobalOnly: Only an Administrator of all services changes the domains.
policyForm.sourcesHelp: How new certificates may enter the service. None ticked: every way.

acme.title: ACME certificates
acme.description: What this service's ACME certificates may use, and the renewal window a new one starts with.

policyForm.noProviders: No certificate authority is set up yet.
policyForm.renewDaysHelp: The default for new ACME certificates of this service, 1 to 60. Empty: Alice's default (30).
policyForm.autoDeployHelp: Forbidden: automatic deployment cannot be switched on for this service's Key Vault bindings and ACME certificates, and those already on wait (with a mark on each website) until it is allowed again.
policyForm.revokeModeHelp: The choice a new incident on this service's certificates starts with.
policyForm.aliceDefault: Alice's default (after every replacement is verified)

notifications.title: E-mails
notifications.description: Who else receives this service's e-mails, saved with the policy. With the box ticked, the Administrators of all services receive them too (platform e-mails always go to them); the addresses below receive them, and so do the owners on the Overview tab.

policyForm.administrators: Administrators of all services receive this service's e-mails

canary.title: Canary deployment
canary.description: Deploy to a few websites first, observe them, and only then deploy to the rest. Applies to every deployment of this service’s keys to two or more websites.
canary.firstHelp: These websites go into the first wave when they are destinations.
canary.holdHelp: How long the first wave is observed, 1m to 24h. Empty: 10m.
canary.intervalHelp: Time between two checks of a website, 15s to 10m. Empty: 30s.
canary.failuresHelp: Failed checks in a row that put the first wave back. Empty: 2.
canary.durationHelp: A number and one unit: s, m or h (for example 90s, 10m, 1h).
canary.checkHelp: An HTTPS request to each website of the first wave, through the new certificate, sent to the website’s own address.
canary.hostHelp: Empty: the website’s own name. Never used as an address.
canary.timeOnly: Without an application check, websites that skip verification are observed by time only.
canary.forbidOverride: Forbid deploying to all at once
canary.forbidOverrideHelp: Without this, a person with a fresh step-up may skip the canary for one deployment.

services.forbiddenMark: Held: its service forbids automatic deployment

owners.title: Owners
owners.description: The people and directory groups responsible for this service. They receive its e-mails; ownership gives no access.
owners.empty: No owners yet. This service's e-mails go to the Administrators and to the extra addresses of its policy.
owners.noReach: Receives e-mails but cannot open this service
owners.noReachGroup: Its members get no access to this service through it
owners.intro: Owners receive this service's e-mails and are shown as responsible for it. Ownership gives no access: give a role on the Access tab for that. A person receives the e-mails when enabled and with an address; a group, through its enabled members seen at sign-in with an address.
owners.noGroups: No directory group is declared yet
owners.reloaded: The list above was reloaded with the latest owners. Check it, then save again.
owners.stepUp: Saving asks for a fresh verification code.

facts.neverDeployed: Alice has not deployed a certificate here yet.
facts.file: The file held {{cert}} at the scan of {{time}}.
facts.fileNever: No scan has read the file yet.
facts.tlsAlice: The website served {{cert}} at {{time}} (checked from Alice).
facts.tlsHelper: The website served {{cert}} at {{time}} (checked from the server itself).
facts.tlsNever: The website has not been checked yet.
facts.untrusted: Its certificate chain is not trusted.
facts.lastProbeFailed: The check at {{time}} could not reach the website.

backoff.flapping: Alice stopped repairing it by itself: another tool kept changing this file. Choose Repair automatically again once that tool is stopped.
backoff.repair_failing: Alice stopped repairing it by itself: the repairs failed. See the deployment history.

cause.binding_repointed: Cause: the binding was changed to another certificate outside Alice.
cause.cert_removed: Cause: the certificate was removed from the server's certificate store. Alice does not put it back; deploy a certificate to this binding.
cause.key_unusable: Cause: Windows cannot use the private key of the certificate. Deploy a certificate to this binding.

drift.autocertrebind: This server runs the AutoCertRebind task, which can bind a certificate by itself and may undo a repair.

summary.inSync_one: Live and verified on {{n}} of {{count}} place
summary.inSync_other: Live and verified on {{n}} of {{count}} places
summary.driftedEnds_one: {{count}} serves another certificate (it ends in {{hours}} h)
summary.driftedEnds_other: {{count}} serve another certificate (the first ends in {{hours}} h)
summary.driftedHelp: Someone or another tool changed what these places have, after Alice had deployed the right certificate. The rows below show what each should have, what Alice last deployed, what the file holds and what the website serves, each with its time.

access.title: Access
access.roleHelp: The role on all services. Without one, the person reaches only the services and environments of their Access.
access.empty: No role on a single service or environment.

none.title: You do not have access to anything yet.

section.description: What this person may reach: the role on all services first, then each role on one service or on every service of an environment.

add.title: Add access
add.stepUp: Adding or removing access asks for a fresh verification code.

explain.title: Effective access
explain.intro: What the roles add up to: each role with the services it reaches now.
explain.cappedTitle: An Administrator role counts as Operator
explain.capped: Single sign-on users may not be Administrators (Settings, single sign-on), so this person's Administrator roles give Operator rights.

service.intro: People who reach this service through a role on the service itself or on every service of its environment.
service.globalNote: Everyone with a role on all services (People & access) reaches this service too.
service.noneDirect: Nobody has a role on this service alone.
service.noneThrough: Nobody has a role through the environment.
service.adminOnly: Only Administrators of all services see who has access.

groupRights.title: Rights through groups
groupRights.intro: Roles this person holds through the directory groups they were in at their last sign-in. Change them on the Groups tab.
groupRights.none: No role through a directory group.

groups.intro: Give a group of an identity provider or a directory a role on services or environments. Its members reach them from their next sign-in, even without a group mapped to a role on all services.

fields.seenHelp: Group values people of this provider or directory had at their last sign-in.
fields.valueHelp: Exactly as the groups claim or the group search returns it; upper and lower case count.
fields.label: Label (optional)

groups.accessIntro: Every member of this group holds these roles from their next sign-in.
groups.noBindings: This group holds no role yet.
groups.deleteText_one: The group and its {{count}} role are removed; its members lose that role at their next request.
groups.deleteText_other: The group and its {{count}} roles are removed; its members lose those roles at their next request.
groups.deleted: Removed. Role bindings removed with it: {{bindings}}; owner entries: {{owners}}.

automation.intro: An automation account is not a person: it never signs in and only holds API tokens, which an Administrator makes here. Its role on all services is Operator, Auditor or none; give it roles on services in its Access.

fields.roleHelp: Never Administrator on all services; give it the Administrator role on the services it needs instead.

automation.disableText_one: Its {{count}} token is revoked for good; enabling the account again does not bring it back.
automation.disableText_other: Its {{count}} tokens are revoked for good; enabling the account again brings none back.
automation.enableText: The account can hold tokens again. Its old tokens stay revoked.
automation.tokenHelp: The token can do what the account's roles allow, and no more. Making one asks for a fresh verification code.
automation.disabledTokens: A disabled automation account holds no tokens. Enable it to make one.

canary.title: Canary deployment
canary.observing: The new certificate is in place and verified; it is under observation before the other websites follow.
canary.roundSummary: {{rounds}} checks so far, {{passes}} passed. Last check: {{result}}.

reason.canary_check_failed: A check of a first-wave website failed too often, so the first wave was put back.
reason.canary_check_unavailable: The checks could not run until the hold ended, so the first wave was put back.
reason.canary_wave1_failed: A first-wave deployment failed, so the first wave was put back.
reason.canary_certificate_revoked: The certificate was revoked or its key marked compromised, so the first wave was put back.
reason.canary_aborted: A person stopped the canary deployment; the first wave was put back.
reason.canary_wave1_incomplete: Not every first-wave website could be deployed within an hour, so the first wave was put back.
reason.canary_preempted_by_incident: A key-compromise incident ended the canary deployment; the first wave keeps the certificate.
reason.license_locked: The licence does not allow changes now: the first wave keeps the certificate, the rest was not deployed.
reason.lock_due: The licence could not be confirmed for an hour: the first wave keeps the certificate, the rest was not deployed.
reason.unverified: The licence could not be verified for an hour: the first wave keeps the certificate, the rest was not deployed.

canary.holdOver: The observation time is over; the next check decides.

skipReason.location_not_found: the website or its server is gone
skipReason.in_progress: another deployment of this website is still running
skipReason.location_unsupported: Alice cannot deploy to this website
skipReason.config_invalid: the server's configuration does not pass its test
skipReason.rescan_needed: the website's files changed; run Discover on its server
skipReason.key_type_mismatch: the website needs another key type
skipReason.service_untrusted: its service does not accept keys from the certificate's service
skipReason.recovery_pending: an earlier change on its server is still being finished

canary.hidden: {{count}} websites outside your services are not shown.
canary.continueHelp: Skips the rest of the observation and deploys to the remaining websites.
canary.abortConfirm: Stop the canary deployment and put the first wave back to the previous certificate? The other websites are not touched.
canary.note: Deploys to {{count}} website(s) first, then waits {{hold}} before the rest.
canary.overrideHelp: Skips the canary for this deployment; asks you to confirm your identity again.
canary.started: Canary deployment started: {{count}} website(s) follow once the first wave passed its observation.
